scenario.name: Google Cloud Mandiant IR & MITRE DFIR — GCP Cloud Audit ServiceAccountKey Creation & Impersonation Chain Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture a busy downtown bank branch with marble teller windows, brass counter bars, and a heavy circular steel vault at the rear. At the front marble counter, a visitor wearing a borrowed courier coat hands the bank teller an official-looking transfer slip to slip past the velvet queue. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the bank teller's station, then smuggles copied records out past the brass teller window in tiny disguised batches. Only when the branch manager reviews the vault camera footage alongside the teller receipt book does the unauthorized vault visit stand out immediately. In this scenario (T1078.004, Google Cloud Mandiant IR & MITRE DFIR, GCP Cloud Audit ServiceAccountKey Creation & Impersonation Chain Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: service Account Impersonation, then persistent User-Managed JSON Key Creation, then bigQuery Table Export. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Service Account Impersonation, then Persistent User-Managed JSON Key Creation, then BigQuery Table Export, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1078.004 across the documented kill chain.
